u1s2: A terminal is the point at which a conductor from a component, device or network comes to an end.
u2s2: A terminal may simply be the end of an electrical wire or it may be fitted with a connector or fastener.
u3s2: In network analysis, terminal means a point at which connections can be made to a network in theory and does not necessarily refer to any physical object.
u4s2: On circuit diagrams, terminals for external connections are denoted by empty circles.
u5s2: All electrochemical cells have two terminals (electrodes) which are referred to as the anode and cathode or positive (+) and negative (–).
u6s2: On many dry batteries, the positive terminal (cathode) is a protruding metal cap, and the negative terminal (anode) is a flat metal disc (see Battery terminal).
u7s2: In a galvanic cell such as a common AA battery, electrons flow from the negative terminal to the positive terminal, while the conventional current is opposite to this.
